public_evidence.observation: ZedTokens represent datastore points-in-time; CheckPermission and relationship mutations return them; at_exact_snapshot and at_least_as_fresh bind later authorization reads to a revision. This is a causal/read fence, not evidence that an unrelated external effect accepts that revision as an atomic precondition.

Authorization models are immutable and callers are encouraged to pin authorization_model_id; HIGHER_CONSISTENCY bypasses query cache. These facts pin model/schema behavior and read freshness but do not expose a tuple-state snapshot token in the checked public surface.

IsAuthorized returns ALLOW/DENY plus determining policy IDs and errors; the checked response contract contains no authorization-store revision token. Determining policy IDs are provenance, not an effect precondition.

getIamPolicy returns etag; setIamPolicy should send the same etag so the write is applied only if policy state still matches. This is mutable-policy optimistic concurrency, not a prior authorization-decision revision.

public_evidence.observation: A PR review can be anchored to commit_id; merge accepts sha that the PR head must match and returns 409 on mismatch. Current public REST supports 2026-03-10 while unversioned requests default to 2022-11-28.

API v1 POST requests can be safely retried with a caller idempotency key; v1 retains keys at least 24h and compares parameters. API v2 extends idempotent keys to POST and DELETE with same-API/account/sandbox scope and a 30-day replay window. Retry identity solves ambiguous execution, not authorization freshness.
Decision logging adds decision_id and policy/bundle metadata for audit/debugging. A decision_id is provenance unless an effect API separately documents it as an enforcement precondition.

high_signal_findings: Authorization decision provenance and mutation exactness are orthogonal axes. A system can expose a strong authorization revision without binding a later external effect, or a strong mutation CAS without exposing the authorization decision revision.

The strongest observed effect boundary in this run is request-local: Kubernetes evaluates current authorization on the mutation request and can independently enforce object version preconditions before persistence.

Approval provenance is strongest when bound to immutable content identity and paired with an effect precondition on that same evolving surface; GitHub commit_id + merge sha is a concrete example, but provider policy still must be re-evaluated/current.

Retry identity is a third independent axis. Stripe idempotency makes ambiguous execution recoverable, but connected Stripe write schema does not currently prove caller-controlled Idempotency-Key exposure.

A model ID, policy ID, decision ID, approval object, or prior allow result must never be upgraded into an authorization lease unless the effect-serving API documents a corresponding enforcement precondition.
acceptance_and_counterexample_tests: SpiceDB ZedToken + exact snapshot => DECISION_REVISION_FENCE, not PRIOR_AUTH_REVISION_EFFECT_GATE.
Synthetic evidence is classified PRIOR_AUTH_REVISION_EFFECT_GATE only when the effect precondition explicitly consumes the prior auth revision.
OpenFGA immutable model ID + HIGHER_CONSISTENCY => POLICY_MODEL_PIN_ONLY.
Kubernetes request authorization + resourceVersion precondition => REQUEST_LOCAL_AUTH_WITH_STATE_CAS.
GitHub review commit_id + merge expected head => APPROVAL_AND_EXACT_INTENT.
Stripe idempotency key replay => IDEMPOTENT_EFFECT_RETRY, not authorization proof.
AWS Verified Permissions determining policy IDs without revision => PROVENANCE_ONLY.
